clue.text: Dissolute chap lay with girl — artistic characters, perhaps

indicators.note: dissolute means loose-living and disordered, so these letters are let loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A rakish man sleeps with a girl, and the pair are cast as colourful characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' means letters, not people: fine handwriting is artistic lettering.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative handwriting produces letters made with artistry, hence artistic characters; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Service provider that keeps device going

definitions.meaning: a large flat serving dish or platter, which provides the service of food at table
a plug-in unit that tops up a phone or other gadget's battery

explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests a utility company, but here it is serving food: the first sense is an old word for a big plate.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a large serving platter; the other is the gadget that replenishes a battery.

clue.text: The setter's trapped by blazing sun, creating restrictions

indicators.note: the setter's contraction is held inside the other pieces, as if caught by them

parts.note: blazing means alight, lit
the setter speaking of himself, 'the setter is', gives I'M

explanation.surface: A setter caught out under a fierce sun finds himself hemmed in by constraints.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves in the third person; 'The setter's' expands to 'the setter is'. 'trapped by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Boundaries or caps that may not be exceeded are restrictions; the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Lack in capacity of processed cyanide ingested

indicators.note: ingested means swallowed, so one piece is taken inside the other
processed means worked over and changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: qua is a Latin-derived word meaning in the capacity of

explanation.surface: A shortfall shows up in how much cyanide, once processed, has been swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' rearranges the poison's letters to INADECY; 'ingested' puts the Latin word inside. 'in capacity of' looks like part of the definition but is the inserted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Inadequacy is a shortfall or insufficiency, so a lack is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Erected hideaway for Middle Eastern money

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means set upright, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lair is an animal's or person's hideaway

explanation.surface: Someone builds a secret retreat to stash cash from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erected' turns LAIR upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The rial is the currency of Iran, Oman and Yemen, all in the Middle East.

clue.text: Iced-up liquid around edges of littoral is transparent

indicators.note: around tells us the shuffled letters surround the pair taken from the shore word
liquid means fluid, not fixed, so the letters of iced-up flow into a new order
edges of picks the first and last letters of littoral

explanation.surface: Ice melting on the shoreline turns into clear water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' looks like a description of melted ice but is the anagram signal; 'around' and 'edges of' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellucid describes something clear enough to see through, a literary synonym for transparent.

clue.text: Dairy product from hog, unusually, in nomadic setting

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the tent

parts.note: a yurt is the round felt tent of Central Asian nomads

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters of hog are reordered

explanation.surface: Something made from a pig, oddly, in a tent on the steppes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the pig to OGH, and 'in' places it inside the nomad's tent.
explanation.definitionFit: It is fermented milk, a standard item in the dairy aisle.

clue.text: My intention is to get back into teetotal society, not having so much claret …

indicators.note: into shows the turned phrase goes inside the abbreviation for the abstainers' group

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a society for those who give up drink

indicators.note: back says the phrase my intention is, as a short phrase, is read in reverse

parts.note: my intention is can be said as I mean

explanation.surface: A drinker vows to rejoin Alcoholics Anonymous and cut down on red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses I MEAN to NAEMI, which goes into AA. 'Claret' is British slang for blood, so the definition means short of blood.
explanation.definitionFit: This condition is a deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin, so the sufferer has too little blood, slangily claret.

clue.text: English in a dry hotel getting large drink quickly

indicators.note: in shows the abbreviation for English is placed among the other pieces

parts.note: TT means teetotal, which is dry
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
a double is a large measure of spirits

explanation.surface: An Englishman in a teetotal hotel somehow gets hold of a big drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts English inside the whole string, not inside 'a dry hotel' alone: it lands just before the drink. TT, for teetotal, is a common crossword abbreviation for dry.
explanation.definitionFit: This military phrase means at a running pace, hence quickly or immediately.

clue.text: … member enrolling in drink society claims

indicators.note: the limb word is enrolling in, so placed inside, the drink word

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
a leg is a member, a limb of the body

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a member joins a drinking club and makes assertions.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading ellipsis links back to 7 Across, whose drink theme it continues.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean asserts something is so without yet proving it, as a verb in the third person.

clue.text: TV network press car crashed — they're high!

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster

indicators.note: crashed means smashed up, so the letters of press car are rearranged

explanation.surface: A television company's press car has been in an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: SKY is a UK satellite TV network; 'crashed' rearranges PRESS CAR into SCRAPERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Very tall buildings are famous for their height; the exclamation plays on 'high' as intoxicated.

clue.text: United tie featuring defensive error

indicators.note: featuring means including, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to tether is to tie up, as a rope ties an animal
OG is an own goal in football, a defender's mistake

explanation.surface: A football match ends level after a defender's blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: OG, football shorthand for own goal, sits after the first T of TETHER. 'United' looks like a team name.
explanation.definitionFit: To be joined as one or acting jointly is to be united; adjective for adjective.

clue.text: Non-essential vote held by Ulster Unionist dividing two wings — section leaving party

indicators.note: dividing means splitting apart, so the inner group goes between the pair of letters

parts.note: L and R stand for the left and right wings

indicators.note: held by puts the voting mark inside the pair of letters

parts.note: UU stands for Ulster Unionist, a Northern Irish political party
a cross, X, marks a vote on a ballot paper

indicators.note: leaving signals that one part goes out of the following word

parts.note: a part is a section of something

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish party vote splits the wings, and a faction quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' and 'dividing' nest the vote inside the unionists inside the wings; 'leaving' takes a section off the party word, leaving its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A luxury is something pleasant but not needed, so a non-essential item; noun matches noun.

clue.text: Source of warm water for UK from Qatar, perhaps — gas is about right

definitions.text: Source of warm water for UK

parts.note: Qatar is an example of a Gulf state, one on the Persian Gulf

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the vapour word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: steam is water in gas form

explanation.surface: Britain gets its heat from Qatar, gas being right about that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Qatar, perhaps' looks like a gas supplier but gives GULF, as a Gulf state.
explanation.definitionFit: This Atlantic current carries tropical water north-east and keeps Britain's climate mild.

clue.text: Bring in part of corn before November

indicators.note: before places the grain part ahead of the letter

parts.note: an ear is the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant
N is November in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Farmers gather in the crop before winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring in' suggests a harvest but means to earn money.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring in money is to make it as income, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Stitching endlessly interrupting boxing — abandoned just over halfway, looking ahead

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking in, so the shortened stitching word goes inside
the fight word is given up after six of its ten letters, just past its midpoint

parts.note: fisticuffs is fighting with fists, boxing

indicators.note: endlessly means with both ends taken off

parts.note: a suture is surgical stitching

explanation.surface: A boxing bout is halted by a cut needing stitches and abandoned soon after half time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned just over halfway' keeps six of the fight word's ten letters, FISTIC; 'endlessly' trims the stitching word to UTUR, and 'interrupting' puts it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futuristic anticipates or depicts the future, so it is forward-looking.

clue.text: Something put in tea as the queen takes it

indicators.note: takes means holds, so the small word is placed inside the conjunction

parts.note: as and when both mean at the time that
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: How Her Majesty likes her tea: with something added.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a fact about royal tea; 'as' is a conjunction meaning at the time that, and 'takes' means holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk or powdered creamer added to tea pales it, making it a product used in tea.

clue.text: Unofficially, where the missing link went?

definitions.meaning: said without preparation or not on the record
a lost cufflink has come away from the shirt sleeve

explanation.walkthrough: 'missing link' suggests evolution, but it is a cufflink that has come away from the sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken remarks made impromptu are informal and unofficial; literally it describes something detached from a sleeve.

clue.text: First lady's underwear from France, I gather, mostly loud

parts.note: F is the international code for France

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: to glean is to gather up bit by bit
F is forte, loud in music

explanation.surface: A tabloid snippet: the first lady's French lingerie is rather loud.
explanation.walkthrough: The first lady is Eve, not a president's wife: in Genesis, she and Adam covered themselves with fig leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Eve, the first woman, wore a leaf of the fig tree as her only garment.

clue.text: Talkative bird, not half lively on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means travelling in reverse, so the shortened word is read backwards
not half means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: animated means lively

explanation.surface: A chatty bird is only partly lively on its return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' may look like slang for 'very', but it means keeping half of ANIMATED, ANIM, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: This spelling names the Asian starling famous for mimicking speech, hence a talkative bird.

clue.text: Wise men entering in appropriate direction in picture

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the travellers go into the two letters

parts.note: the Magi are the Wise Men of the Nativity
E for east, appropriate since the Magi came from the East

explanation.surface: A Nativity scene: the Wise Men arrive from the right quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate direction' is E, east, apt since the Wise Men came from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form a mental image of it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: American election over for Olympian

parts.note: a poll is an election, a vote
O is over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: The US election is done, crowning a new champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests an athlete, but means a god of Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: This god of music and the sun lived on Mount Olympus, so he is one of the Olympians.

clue.text: Fathers, say, wearing specs?

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the bets word wraps round the example abbreviation

parts.note: specs, short for speculations, are bets or gambles
say means for example, EG

explanation.surface: Dads in glasses, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specs' looks like spectacles but is short for speculations, gambles, BETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To father children is to beget them; both are verbs in the third person singular.

clue.text: Strike to reverse disparity in employee's initial sums

indicators.note: to reverse tells us the whole assembled string is read backwards
in places the gap inside the other letters
initial picks the first letter of employee's

parts.note: pots are sums of money, as in pots of cash
a gap is a disparity, as in a pay gap

explanation.surface: Industrial action to close the pay gap in staff wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' applies to everything after it, so the assembled EGAPPOTS is turned round; 'Strike' is the noun, a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt in work, as when workers walk out, so a strike.

clue.text: Not so many going uncovered — it might pour

indicators.note: the top letter of the down entry is taken off, like a lid removed

parts.note: fewer means not so many

explanation.surface: Fewer people go out without cover when rain threatens.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the cover is the top letter, so FEWER loses only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug with a wide mouth is made for pouring water, so it is something that might pour.

clue.text: Kind of diagram featured in Eastern astronomy essentially has weight still

indicators.note: featured in means appearing within, so the diagram name sits between the two letters
essentially picks the central letter, the essence, of astronomy

parts.note: a Venn diagram shows overlapping sets as circles

explanation.surface: Eastern astronomy still uses overlapping circle diagrams and weighs things.
explanation.walkthrough: VENN goes between E and O, the middle letter of 'astronomy', and W follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning at this moment too, as in 'still unsure'.

clue.text: Serial chocolate head going mad for cakes

indicators.note: going mad means losing order, so these letters are scrambled
head picks the first letter of chocolate

explanation.surface: A chocoholic loses their mind over cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: SERIAL plus C, the head of 'chocolate', rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: These are finger-shaped choux pastries filled with cream and iced with chocolate, a kind of small cake.

clue.text: Female traveller and Latin man, finally out of love, need ticket out, being this

definitions.text: Female traveller and Latin man, finally out of love, need ticket out, being this

indicators.note: out means outside, so the ticket word goes round the rest

parts.note: a fare is the price of a ticket, or the ticket itself
a Rom is a Romany, a gypsy traveller

indicators.note: finally out of removes the last letter of the Latin word

parts.note: homo is Latin for man
love in tennis is nil, the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman and a man who have fallen out of love buy tickets out and end up abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: A Rom is a Romany traveller. 'finally out of' drops the last letter of the Latin word, and 'out' wraps the ticket around the rest. The whole clue describes the departing lovers.
explanation.definitionFit: People who have taken a ticket out of their home town are living a long way off, distant from where they belong.
